content: Nicotine lozenges are prescribed to assist individuals in quitting smoking. They belong to a category of medications known as smoking cessation aids. These lozenges deliver nicotine to the body, which helps alleviate withdrawal symptoms and reduces the craving to smoke. Nicotine lozenges are designed to dissolve slowly in the mouth. They should be used as directed on the packaging, typically at least 15 minutes after consuming food or beverages. It is essential to follow the instructions carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the lozenges exactly as prescribed, without exceeding or reducing the recommended dosage or frequency. If you smoke your first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking up, you should use the 4 mg nicotine lozenges. If your first cigarette is smoked more than 30 minutes after waking, the 2 mg lozenges are appropriate. During the first six weeks of treatment, you should use one lozenge every 1 to 2 hours, ensuring you consume at least nine lozenges daily to maximize your chances of quitting. In weeks 7 to 9, reduce the frequency to one lozenge every 2 to 4 hours. By weeks 10 to 12, use one lozenge every 4 to 8 hours. Do not exceed five lozenges within a six-hour period or more than 20 lozenges in a single day. Avoid using more than one lozenge at a time or consecutively, as this may lead to side effects such as hiccups, heartburn, or nausea. To use the lozenge, place it in your mouth and allow it to dissolve slowly, which should take approximately 20 to 30 minutes. Do not chew or swallow the lozenge. Occasionally, move the lozenge from one side of your mouth to the other using your tongue. Avoid eating while the lozenge is in your mouth. Discontinue the use of nicotine lozenges after 12 weeks. If you still feel the need to use them, consult your doctor. This medication may have other uses. Speak with your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before starting nicotine lozenges, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nicotine or any other medications. Do not use nicotine lozenges if you are already using another nicotine replacement therapy, such as patches, gum, inhalers, or nasal sprays. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. This includes non-nicotine smoking cessation aids like bupropion (Wellbutrin) or varenicline (Chantix), as well as medications for depression or asthma. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication dosages after you quit smoking. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using nicotine lozenges, contact your doctor immediately. It is crucial to stop smoking entirely while using nicotine lozenges, as continuing to smoke may result in adverse effects. Seek advice and written resources from your doctor or pharmacist to support your smoking cessation efforts. Combining nicotine lozenges with professional guidance and support increases the likelihood of successfully quitting smoking. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, you may maintain your regular diet while using nicotine lozenges. Nicotine lozenges may cause mild side effects, such as heartburn or a sore throat. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects, such as mouth problems or an irregular or rapid heartbeat, require immediate medical attention. If you experience any unusual symptoms while using this medication, contact your doctor. Store nicotine lozenges in their original container, ensuring it is tightly sealed and kept out of reach of children and pets. Store the medication at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and avoid storing it in the bathroom. If you need to dispose of a lozenge, wrap it in paper before discarding it. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, diarrhea, weakness, or a rapid heartbeat. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor while using nicotine lozenges. If you have any questions about this medication, consult your pharmacist. Nicotine lozenges are available under the brand name Commit®.
